slides: Let's continue with prime numbers. How do we check a bigger number, and what are factors?

slides.say: How do we check a bigger number? We divide it by the primes up to its square root, and no further. Why is that enough? If a number breaks into two factors, they can't both be bigger than its square root, because then their product would be bigger than the number. So one of the factors is at most the root, and we'd find it.
at: We divide it by the primes up to its square root

slides.say: Let's take ninety-one. Nine squared is eighty-one, and ten squared is a hundred, so the root of ninety-one is less than ten. The primes below ten are two, three, five and seven, so we only try those.

Two? Ninety-one is odd, so no. Three? Add the digits. Nine plus one is ten, and ten doesn't divide by three, so no. Five? It doesn't end in zero or five, so no. Seven? Seven times thirteen is ninety-one. So ninety-one is not prime.
at: It doesn't end in zero or five

slides.say: Now a number that is prime, eighty-nine. Its root is less than ten too. Eighty-nine is odd. Its digit sum is seventeen, which doesn't divide by three. It doesn't end in zero or five. And seven times twelve is eighty-four, while seven times thirteen is ninety-one, so seven skips over it. None of them divides it, so eighty-nine is prime.
at: Its root is less than ten too
It doesn't end in zero or five

slides.say: Some numbers look prime but aren't, and the exam loves them. Fifty-one, fifty-seven and eighty-seven all divide by three, because their digit sums are six, twelve and fifteen. Ninety-one and a hundred nineteen both divide by seven.

Two words mean exactly the same thing, divisor and factor. A factor of a number divides it with no remainder. Twenty-eight divides by four, so four is a factor of twenty-eight, or a divisor of twenty-eight. Forty-five divides by nine, so nine is a factor of forty-five.
And a non-example. Six times four is twenty-four, and six times five is thirty, so twenty-eight doesn't divide by six. Six is not a factor of twenty-eight.
at: so twenty-eight doesn't divide by six

slides.say: The word divisor confuses a lot of students. Whenever you see it, replace it with factor. It's the same thing.

A prime factor is a factor that is also a prime. Twenty-eight is two times two times seven, so its prime factors are two and seven. Four is a factor of twenty-eight, but it isn't a prime factor, because four isn't prime.
at: Twenty-eight is two times two times seven

slides.say: A number divides by all its prime factors, and by every combination of them. Take twenty, which is two times two times five. It divides by two and by five, its prime factors. It also divides by four, which is two times two, by ten, which is two times five, and by twenty, which is all of them together.
at: which is two times two, by

slides.say: One more. Eighteen is two times three times three. So it divides by two and by three, by six, which is two times three, by nine, which is three times three, and by eighteen itself. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next part.
